procedure:extensions.pgrst_ddl_watch().name: pgrst_ddl_watch
procedure:extensions.pgrst_ddl_watch().source_code:
DECLARE
  cmd record;
BEGIN
  FOR cmd IN SELECT * FROM pg_event_trigger_ddl_commands()
  LOOP
    IF cmd.command_tag IN (
      'CREATE SCHEMA', 'ALTER SCHEMA'
    , 'CREATE TABLE', 'CREATE TABLE AS', 'SELECT INTO', 'ALTER TABLE'
    , 'CREATE FOREIGN TABLE', 'ALTER FOREIGN TABLE'
    , 'CREATE VIEW', 'ALTER VIEW'
    , 'CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW', 'ALTER MATERIALIZED VIEW'
    , 'CREATE FUNCTION', 'ALTER FUNCTION'
    , 'CREATE TRIGGER'
    , 'CREATE TYPE', 'ALTER TYPE'
    , 'CREATE RULE'
    , 'COMMENT'
    )
    -- don't notify in case of CREATE TEMP table or other objects created on pg_temp
    AND cmd.schema_name is distinct from 'pg_temp'
    THEN
      NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema';
    END IF;
  END LOOP;
END;

procedure:public.assignable_jobs().name: assignable_jobs
procedure:public.assignable_jobs().source_code:
select
    j.id,
    j.title,
    sc.slug,
    q.labor_amount_cents,
    q.customer_fee_cents,
    -- The generated column. Never recomputed anywhere.
    q.total_cents,
    j.requested_service_start,
    j.address_id is not null and j.service_location is not null,
    j.requested_service_start is not null,
    quote_is_current(q.id)
  from jobs j
  join price_quotes q      on q.id = j.price_quote_id
  join service_categories sc on sc.id = j.category_id
  where j.customer_id = auth.uid()
    -- Priced but not yet out with anyone. A published job can also be assigned
    -- directly — that is the conversion case — so it is included too.
    and j.status in ('priced', 'published')
    -- Nothing with a live booking: that job already has a pro.
    and not exists (
      select 1 from bookings b
       where b.job_id = j.id and not booking_is_terminal(b.status)
    )
  order by j.updated_at desc;

procedure:public.begin_stripe_event(text.name: begin_stripe_event
procedure:public.begin_stripe_event(text.definition:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.begin_stripe_event(p_event_id text, p_type text, p_livemode boolean, p_api_version text DEFAULT NULL::text, p_payload jsonb DEFAULT NULL::jsonb)
 RETURNS boolean
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public'
AS $function$
declare
  v_status text;
begin
  if not is_trusted_caller() then
    raise exception 'Only the server may record a Stripe event'
      using errcode = '42501';
  end if;

  insert into stripe_events (event_id, type, livemode, api_version, payload, attempts)
  values (p_event_id, p_type, p_livemode, p_api_version, p_payload, 1)
  on conflict (event_id) do update
     set attempts = stripe_events.attempts + 1
  returning status into v_status;

  -- Already done. The retry is acknowledged and nothing happens again.
  return v_status is distinct from 'processed';
end;
$function$

procedure:public.booking_terminal_at(uui.name: booking_terminal_at
procedure:public.booking_terminal_at(uui.source_code:
select case
    when not booking_is_terminal(b.status) then null
    else coalesce(
      -- The first transition INTO a terminal status. Immutable once written,
      -- and unaffected by any later edit to the booking row.
      (select min(h.created_at)
         from booking_status_history h
        where h.booking_id = b.id
          and booking_is_terminal(h.new_status)),
      b.completed_at,
      b.cancelled_at,
      b.updated_at)
  end
  from bookings b
  where b.id = p_booking_id;
procedure:public.booking_terminal_at(uui.definition:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.booking_terminal_at(p_booking_id uuid)
 RETURNS timestamp with time zone
 LANGUAGE sql
 STABLE SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public'
AS $function$
  select case
    when not booking_is_terminal(b.status) then null
    else coalesce(
      -- The first transition INTO a terminal status. Immutable once written,
      -- and unaffected by any later edit to the booking row.
      (select min(h.created_at)
         from booking_status_history h
        where h.booking_id = b.id
          and booking_is_terminal(h.new_status)),
      b.completed_at,
      b.cancelled_at,
      b.updated_at)
  end
  from bookings b
  where b.id = p_booking_id;
$function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.bookings_protect_authoritative()
 RETURNS trigger
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $function$
begin
  if is_trusted_context() or is_admin() then
    -- NEW is NULL in a BEFORE DELETE trigger, and returning NULL CANCELS the
    -- operation. Returning `new` unconditionally therefore made every delete a
    -- silent no-op — no error, no row removed. Return the right record per op.
    return case when tg_op = 'DELETE' then old else new end;
  end if;
  raise exception 'Bookings are modified only through the protected transition functions'
    using errcode = '42501';
end;
$function$

procedure:public.browse_pros(text,uuid[].argument_defaults: NULL::text, NULL::uuid[], NULL::public.geography, NULL::integer, NULL::numeric, NULL::integer, false, NULL::timestamp with time zone, 60, 'best_fit'::public.pro_sort_key, 40, 0
procedure:public.browse_pros(text,uuid[].source_code:
with base as (
    select
      v.*,
      -- Nearest service area, used for distance only. Never returned as
      -- geometry, and rounded below so it cannot be used to triangulate.
      (select min(st_distance(sa.centroid, p_near))
         from pro_service_areas sa
        where sa.pro_id = v.pro_id and sa.is_active)::int as raw_distance,
      exists (select 1 from pro_favourites f
               where f.customer_id = auth.uid() and f.pro_id = v.pro_id) as fav
    from pro_public_profiles v
    where v.is_accepting_work
      and (p_category_slug is null or exists (
            select 1 from pro_public_categories c
             where c.pro_id = v.pro_id and c.slug = p_category_slug))
      and (p_skill_ids is null or cardinality(p_skill_ids) = 0 or not exists (
            select 1 from unnest(p_skill_ids) req(skill_id)
             where not exists (
               select 1 from pro_public_skills s
                where s.pro_id = v.pro_id and s.skill_id = req.skill_id)))
      and (not p_requires_licence or v.is_licensed_and_insured)
      and (p_min_experience is null or v.years_experience >= p_min_experience)
      -- Rating filters use the neutral baseline, so a qualified new pro is not
      -- silently excluded by a "4 stars and up" filter for having no reviews.
      and (p_min_rating is null or v.effective_rating >= p_min_rating)
  ),
  filtered as (
    select b.*,
      case
        when p_available_from is null then true
        else pro_is_available(b.pro_id, p_available_from, p_duration_minutes, 'standard')
      end as available
    from base b
    where p_near is null
       or p_max_distance_m is null
       or (b.raw_distance is not null and b.raw_distance <= p_max_distance_m)
  )
  select
    f.pro_id,
    f.display_name,
    f.avatar_path,
    f.bio,
    f.years_experience,
    f.is_verified,
    f.is_licensed_and_insured,
    -- Null for an unrated pro, so the client shows "New to Tarea" rather than
    -- rendering a zero.
    case when f.rating_count > 0 then f.rating_average end,
    f.rating_count,
    f.completed_jobs_count,
    f.is_new_pro,
    -- Rounded to the nearest 100 m. Enough to sort and to say "about 4 km";
    -- not enough to locate anybody.
    case when f.raw_distance is null then null
         else (round(f.raw_distance / 100.0) * 100)::int end,
    f.available,
    f.fav,
    pro_fit_score(f.rating_average, f.rating_count, f.completed_jobs_count,
                  f.years_experience, f.raw_distance, false,
                  f.is_licensed_and_insured)::int
  from filtered f
  where f.available or p_available_from is null
  order by
    case when p_sort = 'distance'     then f.raw_distance end asc nulls last,
    case when p_sort = 'rating'       then f.effective_rating end desc nulls last,
    case when p_sort = 'experience'   then f.years_experience end desc nulls last,
    case when p_sort = 'availability' then (case when f.available then 0 else 1 end) end asc,
    case when p_sort = 'best_fit'     then
      pro_fit_score(f.rating_average, f.rating_count, f.completed_jobs_count,
                    f.years_experience, f.raw_distance, false,
                    f.is_licensed_and_insured) end desc nulls last,
    f.pro_id
  limit greatest(least(coalesce(p_limit, 40), 100), 1)
  offset greatest(coalesce(p_offset, 0), 0);
procedure:public.browse_pros(text,uuid[].definition:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.browse_pros(p_category_slug text DEFAULT NULL::text, p_skill_ids uuid[] DEFAULT NULL::uuid[], p_near public.geography DEFAULT NULL::public.geography, p_max_distance_m integer DEFAULT NULL::integer, p_min_rating numeric DEFAULT NULL::numeric, p_min_experience integer DEFAULT NULL::integer, p_requires_licence boolean DEFAULT false, p_available_from timestamp with time zone DEFAULT NULL::timestamp with time zone, p_duration_minutes integer DEFAULT 60, p_sort public.pro_sort_key DEFAULT 'best_fit'::public.pro_sort_key, p_limit integer DEFAULT 40, p_offset integer DEFAULT 0)
 RETURNS TABLE(pro_id uuid, display_name text, avatar_path text, bio text, years_experience integer, is_verified boolean, is_licensed_and_insured boolean, rating_average numeric, rating_count integer, completed_jobs_count integer, is_new_pro boolean, distance_meters integer, is_available boolean, is_favourite boolean, fit_score integer)
 LANGUAGE sql
 STABLE SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public'
AS $function$
  with base as (
    select
      v.*,
      -- Nearest service area, used for distance only. Never returned as
      -- geometry, and rounded below so it cannot be used to triangulate.
      (select min(st_distance(sa.centroid, p_near))
         from pro_service_areas sa
        where sa.pro_id = v.pro_id and sa.is_active)::int as raw_distance,
      exists (select 1 from pro_favourites f
               where f.customer_id = auth.uid() and f.pro_id = v.pro_id) as fav
    from pro_public_profiles v
    where v.is_accepting_work
      and (p_category_slug is null or exists (
            select 1 from pro_public_categories c
             where c.pro_id = v.pro_id and c.slug = p_category_slug))
      and (p_skill_ids is null or cardinality(p_skill_ids) = 0 or not exists (
            select 1 from unnest(p_skill_ids) req(skill_id)
             where not exists (
               select 1 from pro_public_skills s
                where s.pro_id = v.pro_id and s.skill_id = req.skill_id)))
      and (not p_requires_licence or v.is_licensed_and_insured)
      and (p_min_experience is null or v.years_experience >= p_min_experience)
      -- Rating filters use the neutral baseline, so a qualified new pro is not
      -- silently excluded by a "4 stars and up" filter for having no reviews.
      and (p_min_rating is null or v.effective_rating >= p_min_rating)
  ),
  filtered as (
    select b.*,
      case
        when p_available_from is null then true
        else pro_is_available(b.pro_id, p_available_from, p_duration_minutes, 'standard')
      end as available
    from base b
    where p_near is null
       or p_max_distance_m is null
       or (b.raw_distance is not null and b.raw_distance <= p_max_distance_m)
  )
  select
    f.pro_id,
    f.display_name,
    f.avatar_path,
    f.bio,
    f.years_experience,
    f.is_verified,
    f.is_licensed_and_insured,
    -- Null for an unrated pro, so the client shows "New to Tarea" rather than
    -- rendering a zero.
    case when f.rating_count > 0 then f.rating_average end,
    f.rating_count,
    f.completed_jobs_count,
    f.is_new_pro,
    -- Rounded to the nearest 100 m. Enough to sort and to say "about 4 km";
    -- not enough to locate anybody.
    case when f.raw_distance is null then null
         else (round(f.raw_distance / 100.0) * 100)::int end,
    f.available,
    f.fav,
    pro_fit_score(f.rating_average, f.rating_count, f.completed_jobs_count,
                  f.years_experience, f.raw_distance, false,
                  f.is_licensed_and_insured)::int
  from filtered f
  where f.available or p_available_from is null
  order by
    case when p_sort = 'distance'     then f.raw_distance end asc nulls last,
    case when p_sort = 'rating'       then f.effective_rating end desc nulls last,
    case when p_sort = 'experience'   then f.years_experience end desc nulls last,
    case when p_sort = 'availability' then (case when f.available then 0 else 1 end) end asc,
    case when p_sort = 'best_fit'     then
      pro_fit_score(f.rating_average, f.rating_count, f.completed_jobs_count,
                    f.years_experience, f.raw_distance, false,
                    f.is_licensed_and_insured) end desc nulls last,
    f.pro_id
  limit greatest(least(coalesce(p_limit, 40), 100), 1)
  offset greatest(coalesce(p_offset, 0), 0);
$function$
procedure:public.browse_pros(text,uuid[].comment: Browse Pros. Reads only pro_public_profiles, returns no geometry, and rounds distance to 100 m. Rating filters use the neutral baseline so a qualified new pro is not excluded for having no reviews. There is no price sort: Tarea sets the labor price.

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.chat_messages_are_immutable()
 RETURNS trigger
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $function$
begin
  -- Trusted contexts still pass, so an admin erasure of a user's account and
  -- the cascade from deleting a booking are not blocked by this.
  if is_trusted_context() or is_admin() then
    return coalesce(new, old);
  end if;
  raise exception 'A sent message cannot be edited or deleted'
    using errcode = '42501';
end;
$function$

procedure:public.claim_guest_photo_delet.name: claim_guest_photo_deletions
procedure:public.claim_guest_photo_delet.source_code:
begin
  return query
  with claimed as (
    select d.id
      from guest_photo_deletions d
     where d.deleted_at is null
       -- Backoff: a row that just failed is not retried on the very next tick.
       and (d.last_try_at is null or d.last_try_at < now() - interval '5 minutes')
       -- Give up automatically after 20 attempts rather than retrying forever.
       -- The row stays pending and visible to the stuck-rows view.
       and d.attempts < 20
     order by d.enqueued_at
     limit p_limit
     for update skip locked
  )
  update guest_photo_deletions g
     set attempts    = g.attempts + 1,
         last_try_at = now()
    from claimed c
   where g.id = c.id
  returning g.id, g.bucket_id, g.path;
end;

procedure:public.claim_outbox_events(int.name: claim_outbox_events
procedure:public.claim_outbox_events(int.source_code:
begin
  if not is_trusted_context() then
    raise exception 'Only the dispatcher may claim notifications'
      using errcode = '42501';
  end if;

  return query
  with claimed as (
    select o.id
      from notification_outbox o
     where o.available_at <= now()
       and (
         o.status = 'pending'
         -- A worker that died mid-flight left this row claimed. The lease is
         -- what lets it be picked up again; without one, a single crash would
         -- strand the alert forever.
         or (o.status = 'dispatching' and o.updated_at < now() - p_lease)
       )
     order by o.available_at, o.id
     limit greatest(coalesce(p_limit, 25), 1)
     for update skip locked
  )
  update notification_outbox o
     set status = 'dispatching',
         attempts = o.attempts + 1,
         updated_at = now()
    from claimed c
   where o.id = c.id
  returning o.*;
end;

procedure:public.cleanup_expired_guest_d.name: cleanup_expired_guest_data
procedure:public.cleanup_expired_guest_d.source_code:
declare
  v_jobs     bigint := 0;
  v_photos   bigint := 0;
  v_sessions bigint := 0;
begin
  -- Enqueue and delete in ONE statement.
  --
  -- Every branch of a data-modifying CTE sees the same snapshot, so the insert
  -- reads storage.objects and jobs as they were when the statement began — the
  -- delete in the sibling branch cannot pull rows out from under it. That makes
  -- the durability guarantee structural rather than a matter of the two
  -- statements happening to agree.
  --
  -- An earlier version used a temporary table declared ON COMMIT DROP, which
  -- was worse in two ways: the temp table only vanished at transaction end, so
  -- calling this function twice in one transaction failed outright; and the
  -- enqueue and delete were separate statements, each free to see a different
  -- snapshot.
  --
  -- Two independent conditions, as before: the row must carry a guest timer AND
  -- belong to an account that is still anonymous. A draft whose owner verified
  -- had its timer cleared by the trigger and also fails the second test, so
  -- permanent customer data is unreachable here even if a timer were somehow
  -- left behind.
  with doomed as (
    select j.id
      from jobs j
      join profiles p on p.id = j.customer_id
     where j.guest_expires_at is not null
       and j.guest_expires_at <= now()
       and p.is_anonymous
       and j.status in ('draft', 'pending_diagnosis', 'priced')
  ),
  queued as (
    insert into guest_photo_deletions (bucket_id, path, job_id)
    select o.bucket_id, o.name, d.id
      from storage.objects o
      join doomed d on split_part(o.name, '/', 1) = d.id::text
     where o.bucket_id = 'job-photos'
    on conflict (bucket_id, path) do nothing
    returning 1
  ),
  gone as (
    delete from jobs where id in (select id from doomed) returning 1
  )
  select (select count(*) from gone), (select count(*) from queued)
    into v_jobs, v_photos;

  -- An empty guest account with no activity is itself expired data. Deleting
  -- the auth user cascades to the profile. Anything that ever became permanent
  -- is excluded by is_anonymous; anything with a job or a booking is excluded
  -- by the not-exists.
  with dead as (
    select p.id
      from profiles p
     where p.is_anonymous
       and p.created_at < now() - interval '48 hours'
       and not exists (select 1 from jobs j where j.customer_id = p.id)
       and not exists (select 1 from bookings b where b.customer_id = p.id)
  ),
  gone as (
    delete from auth.users u where u.id in (select id from dead) returning 1
  )
  select count(*) into v_sessions from gone;

  return query select v_jobs, v_photos, v_sessions;
end;

AS $function$
declare

  -- was worse in two ways: the temp table only vanished at transaction end, so
  -- calling this function twice in one transaction failed outright; and the
  -- enqueue and delete were separate statements, each free to see a different
  -- snapshot.

  -- belong to an account that is still anonymous. A draft whose owner verified
  -- had its timer cleared by the trigger and also fails the second test, so

  with doomed as (

      from jobs j
      join profiles p on p.id = j.customer_id
     where j.guest_expires_at is not null
       and j.guest_expires_at <= now()
       and p.is_anonymous
       and j.status in ('draft', 'pending_diagnosis', 'priced')
  ),
  queued as (
    insert into guest_photo_deletions (bucket_id, path, job_id)
    select o.bucket_id, o.name, d.id
      from storage.objects o
      join doomed d on split_part(o.name, '/', 1) = d.id::text
     where o.bucket_id = 'job-photos'
    on conflict (bucket_id, path) do nothing
    returning 1
  ),
  gone as (
    delete from jobs where id in (select id from doomed) returning 1
  )
  select (select count(*) from gone), (select count(*) from queued)
    into v_jobs, v_photos;

  -- An empty guest account with no activity is itself expired data. Deleting
  -- the auth user cascades to the profile. Anything that ever became permanent

  with dead as (

      from profiles p
     where p.is_anonymous
       and p.created_at < now() - interval '48 hours'

  return query select v_jobs, v_photos, v_sessions;
end;
$function$
procedure:public.cleanup_expired_guest_d.comment: Phase 1: records every photograph of an expiring guest draft in guest_photo_deletions and deletes the drafts, atomically. Does NOT touch Storage — Supabase forbids direct DML on storage.objects. The caller drains the queue through the Storage API.

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.complete_outbox_event(p_id uuid, p_title text, p_body text, p_route text DEFAULT NULL::text)
 RETURNS void
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public'
AS $function$
declare
  v_event notification_outbox%rowtype;
begin
  if not is_trusted_context() then
    raise exception 'Only the dispatcher may complete notifications'
      using errcode = '42501';
  end if;

  select * into v_event from notification_outbox where id = p_id;
  if not found then
    raise exception 'No such outbox event' using errcode = 'no_data_found';
  end if;

  insert into notifications (recipient_user_id, event_type, title, body,
                             entity_type, entity_id, action_route, priority,
                             outbox_id)
  values (v_event.recipient_user_id, v_event.event_type, p_title, p_body,
          v_event.entity_type, v_event.entity_id, p_route, v_event.priority,
          v_event.id)
  on conflict (outbox_id) do nothing;

  update notification_outbox
     set status = 'dispatched',
         dispatched_at = now(),
         last_error = null,
         updated_at = now()
   where id = p_id;
end;
$function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.deactivate_my_account(p_reason text DEFAULT NULL::text)
 RETURNS void
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public'
AS $function$
declare
  v_live int;
begin
  if auth.uid() is null then
    raise exception 'Sign in first' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;

  select count(*) into v_live
    from bookings b
   where (b.customer_id = auth.uid() or b.pro_id = auth.uid())
     and not booking_is_terminal(b.status);

  if v_live > 0 then
    raise exception
      'You have % booking(s) still in progress. Finish or cancel them first.', v_live
      using errcode = 'invalid_parameter_value', hint = 'live_bookings';
  end if;

  update profiles
     set is_active = false,
         deactivated_at = now()
   where id = auth.uid();

  -- A deactivated pro stops being offered work immediately.
  update pro_profiles
     set is_accepting_work = false
   where profile_id = auth.uid();

  insert into audit_events (actor_id, actor_kind, action, entity_type, entity_id, metadata)
  values (auth.uid(), 'user', 'account.deactivated', 'profile', auth.uid(),
          jsonb_build_object('reason', left(coalesce(p_reason, ''), 500)));
end;
$function$
procedure:public.deactivate_my_account(t.comment: Self-service deactivation. Refuses while a booking is live, and deletes nothing — erasure is an admin decision.

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.detach_payment_method_by_stripe_id(p_stripe_pm_id text)
 RETURNS void
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public'
AS $function$
declare
  v_row payment_methods%rowtype;
begin
  if not is_trusted_caller() then
    raise exception 'Only the server may detach a payment method'
      using errcode = '42501';
  end if;

  select * into v_row from payment_methods
   where stripe_payment_method_id = p_stripe_pm_id;

  if not found then
    return;  -- nothing to do; a detach we never knew about is not an error
  end if;

  update payment_methods
     set detached_at = coalesce(detached_at, now()),
         is_default  = false,
         updated_at  = now()
   where id = v_row.id;

  -- Removing the default leaves the person with none, which would silently
  -- break the next booking. Promote the most recently saved survivor.
  if v_row.is_default then
    update payment_methods
       set is_default = true, updated_at = now()
     where id = (
       select id from payment_methods
        where profile_id = v_row.profile_id
          and detached_at is null
        order by created_at desc
        limit 1
     );
  end if;
end;
$function$

procedure:public.effective_rating(numeri.definition:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.effective_rating(p_average numeric, p_count integer)
 RETURNS numeric
 LANGUAGE sql
 IMMUTABLE
AS $function$
  select case
    when p_count is null or p_count = 0 then neutral_rating_baseline()
    else (
      (coalesce(p_average, neutral_rating_baseline()) * least(p_count, rating_confidence_threshold())
        + neutral_rating_baseline() * greatest(rating_confidence_threshold() - p_count, 0))
      / rating_confidence_threshold()
    )
  end;
$function$
procedure:public.effective_rating(numeri.comment: Bayesian-style blend toward a neutral baseline. Prevents both a lucky first review and a cold start from dominating.

procedure:public.eligible_pros_for_job(u.name: eligible_pros_for_job
procedure:public.eligible_pros_for_job(u.source_code:
with job as (
    select j.*, coalesce(j.requires_license_insurance, false) as needs_docs
    from jobs j where j.id = p_job_id
  )
  select
    p.profile_id,
    st_distance(a.centroid, job.service_location)::int
  from job
  join pro_profiles p
    on p.approval_state = 'approved'
   and p.suspended_at is null
   and p.is_accepting_work
  join pro_service_categories psc
    on psc.pro_id = p.profile_id
   and psc.category_id = job.category_id
   and psc.approved_at is not null
  join lateral (
    select sa.centroid
    from pro_service_areas sa
    where sa.pro_id = p.profile_id and sa.is_active
    order by st_distance(sa.centroid, job.service_location) nulls last
    limit 1
  ) a on true
  where pro_serves_point(p.profile_id, job.service_location, job.final_priority)
    and (not job.needs_docs or pro_is_licensed_and_insured(p.profile_id))
    and (
      cardinality(job.required_skill_ids) = 0
      or not exists (
        select 1 from unnest(job.required_skill_ids) req(skill_id)
        where not exists (
          select 1 from pro_skills ps
          where ps.pro_id = p.profile_id and ps.skill_id = req.skill_id
        )
      )
    )
    and not pro_at_workload_limit(p.profile_id)
    -- Explicitly paused pros are out even if still flagged as accepting work.
    and not exists (
      select 1 from pro_scheduling_settings s
      where s.pro_id = p.profile_id
        and s.is_paused
        and (s.paused_until is null or s.paused_until > now())
    )
    and not users_are_blocked(p.profile_id, job.customer_id)
    and p.profile_id <> job.customer_id
    -- Onboarding is incomplete until every approved service is priced. A pro
    -- here cannot be paid for approved extra work, so offering them the job
    -- would set up a failure at the worst moment — mid-job, with the customer
    -- waiting.
    --
    -- THIS CLAUSE IS THE ONLY ADDITION. Everything above is reproduced verbatim
    -- from 20260811110000; an earlier draft of this migration rewrote the body
    -- from a TRUNCATED dump and silently dropped the paused, blocked-user and
    -- self-booking clauses. A publication test caught it — a blocked pro became
    -- eligible again — but only because that test existed.
    and pro_rates_complete(p.profile_id);

procedure:public.guest_cleanup_health().name: guest_cleanup_health
procedure:public.guest_cleanup_health().source_code:
with q as (
    select
      count(*) filter (where deleted_at is null)                    as pending,
      count(*) filter (where deleted_at is null and attempts >= 5)  as stuck,
      min(enqueued_at) filter (where deleted_at is null)            as oldest_pending,
      max(deleted_at)                                               as last_deletion_at
    from guest_photo_deletions
  ),
  -- Drafts that are already past their window and still present. A rising
  -- number here means phase 1 is not running at all — which the queue counts
  -- alone would not reveal, because an unrun cleanup enqueues nothing and
  -- therefore looks perfectly healthy.
  d as (
    select count(*) as expired_drafts
      from jobs j
      join profiles p on p.id = j.customer_id
     where j.guest_expires_at is not null
       and j.guest_expires_at <= now() - interval '2 hours'
       and p.is_anonymous
       and j.status in ('draft', 'pending_diagnosis', 'priced')
  )
  select
    (q.stuck = 0
     and coalesce(q.oldest_pending > now() - interval '24 hours', true)
     and d.expired_drafts = 0),
    case
      when d.expired_drafts > 0
        then 'expired guest drafts are not being collected'
      when q.stuck > 0
        then 'photographs are failing deletion repeatedly'
      when q.oldest_pending <= now() - interval '24 hours'
        then 'photographs have been pending deletion for over a day'
      else null
    end,
    q.pending, q.stuck, q.oldest_pending, q.last_deletion_at, d.expired_drafts
  from q, d;
procedure:public.guest_cleanup_health().definition:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.guest_cleanup_health()
 RETURNS TABLE(healthy boolean, reason text, pending bigint, stuck bigint, oldest_pending timestamp with time zone, last_deletion_at timestamp with time zone, expired_drafts bigint)
 LANGUAGE sql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public'
AS $function$
  with q as (
    select
      count(*) filter (where deleted_at is null)                    as pending,
      count(*) filter (where deleted_at is null and attempts >= 5)  as stuck,
      min(enqueued_at) filter (where deleted_at is null)            as oldest_pending,
      max(deleted_at)                                               as last_deletion_at
    from guest_photo_deletions
  ),
  -- Drafts that are already past their window and still present. A rising
  -- number here means phase 1 is not running at all — which the queue counts
  -- alone would not reveal, because an unrun cleanup enqueues nothing and
  -- therefore looks perfectly healthy.
  d as (
    select count(*) as expired_drafts
      from jobs j
      join profiles p on p.id = j.customer_id
     where j.guest_expires_at is not null
       and j.guest_expires_at <= now() - interval '2 hours'
       and p.is_anonymous
       and j.status in ('draft', 'pending_diagnosis', 'priced')
  )
  select
    (q.stuck = 0
     and coalesce(q.oldest_pending > now() - interval '24 hours', true)
     and d.expired_drafts = 0),
    case
      when d.expired_drafts > 0
        then 'expired guest drafts are not being collected'
      when q.stuck > 0
        then 'photographs are failing deletion repeatedly'
      when q.oldest_pending <= now() - interval '24 hours'
        then 'photographs have been pending deletion for over a day'
      else null
    end,
    q.pending, q.stuck, q.oldest_pending, q.last_deletion_at, d.expired_drafts
  from q, d;
$function$
procedure:public.guest_cleanup_health().comment: Answers "is guest data actually being deleted?" without trusting the scheduler. Checks the queue AND the population of overdue drafts, because a cleanup that never runs enqueues nothing and so looks healthy by queue depth alone.

-- True inside a SECURITY DEFINER routine owned by postgres, and for a
  -- service-role connection from an Edge Function.

procedure:public.job_pro_results_sorted(.name: job_pro_results_sorted
procedure:public.job_pro_results_sorted(.source_code:
select r.*
  from job_pro_results r
  where r.job_id = p_job_id
  order by
    r.result_group,
    case p_sort
      when 'distance'     then coalesce(r.distance_meters, 2147483647)
      -- A finite sentinel, not 'infinity': that timestamp is a valid value but
      -- cannot be cast to bigint, which errored at runtime rather than at
      -- migration time. Pros with no confirmed slot sort last.
      when 'availability' then coalesce(extract(epoch from r.available_start_at)::bigint, 253402300799)
      else null
    end asc nulls last,
    case p_sort
      when 'best_fit'   then r.fit_score + (case when r.is_new_pro then 3 else 0 end)
      when 'rating'     then (r.effective_rating * 20)::int
      when 'experience' then r.years_experience
      else null
    end desc nulls last,
    -- Stable tiebreak so two loads never disagree.
    r.match_id;

 SECURITY DEFINER

begin
  if new.status is distinct from old.status

procedure:public.link_stripe_customer(uu.name: link_stripe_customer
procedure:public.link_stripe_customer(uu.definition:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.link_stripe_customer(p_profile_id uuid, p_stripe_customer_id text, p_livemode boolean DEFAULT false)
 RETURNS void
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public'
AS $function$
begin
  if not is_trusted_caller() then
    raise exception 'Only the server may link a Stripe customer'
      using errcode = '42501';
  end if;

  if p_stripe_customer_id is null or p_stripe_customer_id !~ '^cus_' then
    raise exception 'That is not a Stripe customer id'
      using errcode = 'invalid_parameter_value', hint = 'bad_customer_id';
  end if;

  -- Re-linking is allowed and idempotent, but REPOINTING is not: a profile that
  -- already maps to one Stripe customer must never be silently moved to
  -- another, because the saved cards would come with it.
  insert into stripe_customers (profile_id, stripe_customer_id, livemode)
  values (p_profile_id, p_stripe_customer_id, coalesce(p_livemode, false))
  on conflict (profile_id) do update
     set updated_at = now()
   where stripe_customers.stripe_customer_id = excluded.stripe_customer_id;

  if not found then
    raise exception 'That profile is already linked to a different Stripe customer'
      using errcode = 'unique_violation', hint = 'already_linked';
  end if;
end;
$function$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.mark_notifications_read(p_ids uuid[] DEFAULT NULL::uuid[])
 RETURNS integer
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public'
AS $function$
declare
  v_count int;
begin
  if auth.uid() is null then
    raise exception 'Sign in first' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;

  update notifications
     set read_at = coalesce(read_at, now()),
         seen_at = coalesce(seen_at, now())
   where recipient_user_id = auth.uid()
     and read_at is null
     -- Null means "everything unread". A supplied list is still filtered by
     -- recipient, so passing somebody else's ids marks nothing.
     and (p_ids is null or id = any(p_ids));

  get diagnostics v_count = row_count;
  return v_count;
end;
$function$
procedure:public.mark_notifications_read.comment: Marks the caller's own unread notifications read. Ids from another recipient match nothing rather than erroring.

procedure:public.my_conversations_page(t.argument_defaults: now(), 20, NULL::timestamp with time zone, NULL::uuid
procedure:public.my_conversations_page(t.source_code:
with visible as (
    select
      c.id as cid,
      c.booking_id as bid,
      b.status as bstatus,
      b.customer_id, b.pro_id, b.job_id, b.category_id,
      c.customer_last_read_at, c.pro_last_read_at,
      c.created_at as conv_created_at,
      (select max(m.created_at) from chat_messages m
        where m.conversation_id = c.id and m.created_at <= p_as_of) as last_at
    from conversations c
    join bookings b on b.id = c.booking_id
    where b.customer_id = auth.uid() or b.pro_id = auth.uid()
  ),
  keyed as (
    -- A conversation with no messages yet still needs a position, or it would
    -- be invisible to a paged list. Its creation time is the natural one.
    select v.*, coalesce(v.last_at, v.conv_created_at) as sort_key
    from visible v
  )
  select
    k.cid,
    k.bid,
    k.bstatus,
    not chat_sending_open(k.bid),
    chat_sending_closes_at(k.bid),
    case when k.customer_id = auth.uid() then k.pro_id else k.customer_id end,
    cp.display_name,
    cp.avatar_path,
    j.title,
    sc.name,
    k.last_at,
    (select m.body from chat_messages m
      where m.conversation_id = k.cid and m.created_at <= p_as_of
      order by m.created_at desc, m.id desc limit 1),
    (select count(*)::int from chat_messages m
      where m.conversation_id = k.cid
        and m.sender_id <> auth.uid()
        and m.created_at <= p_as_of
        and m.created_at > coalesce(
              case when k.customer_id = auth.uid()
                   then k.customer_last_read_at else k.pro_last_read_at end,
              '-infinity'::timestamptz)),
    k.sort_key
  from keyed k
  left join lateral chat_counterpart(k.cid) cp on true
  left join jobs j on j.id = k.job_id
  left join service_categories sc on sc.id = k.category_id
  where p_before_at is null
     or (k.sort_key, k.cid) < (p_before_at, coalesce(p_before_id, '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'::uuid))
  order by k.sort_key desc, k.cid desc
  limit least(greatest(coalesce(p_limit, 20), 1), 100);

procedure:public.pro_assignment_summary(.name: pro_assignment_summary
procedure:public.pro_assignment_summary(.source_code:
select
    b.id,
    b.job_id,
    b.status,
    j.assignment_mode,
    j.title,
    j.description,
    sc.name,
    j.estimated_duration_minutes,
    q.labor_amount_cents,
    q.expected_payout_cents,
    q.currency,
    b.scheduled_start,
    b.scheduled_end,
    b.decline_deadline,

    -- Measured against the COARSENED job location, never the exact one, so the
    -- number cannot be sharpened by comparing it with a second reading.
    (round(
       (select min(st_distance(sa.centroid, j.approx_location))
          from pro_service_areas sa
         where sa.pro_id = b.pro_id and sa.is_active) / 100.0
     ) * 100)::int,

    case
      when b.status in ('confirmed', 'en_route', 'in_progress',
                        'completion_submitted', 'completed', 'disputed')
      then concat_ws(', ', a.line1, a.line2, a.city, a.state, a.postal_code)
    end,

    -- A first name only, and only once they are coming. Enough to greet
    -- somebody at a door; not a record to keep.
    case
      when b.status in ('confirmed', 'en_route', 'in_progress',
                        'completion_submitted', 'completed', 'disputed')
      then split_part(btrim(p.full_name), ' ', 1)
    end

  from bookings b
  join jobs j                on j.id = b.job_id
  join price_quotes q        on q.id = b.price_quote_id
  join service_categories sc on sc.id = b.category_id
  join profiles p            on p.id = b.customer_id
  left join user_addresses a on a.id = b.address_id
  -- The authorisation. A pro sees a booking only if it is theirs; there is no
  -- parameter or role that widens this.
  where b.id = p_booking_id
    and b.pro_id = auth.uid();

procedure:public.pro_fit_score(numeric,i.name: pro_fit_score
procedure:public.pro_fit_score(numeric,i.source_code:
select least(100, greatest(0, (
      -- Rating, blended (0-40)
      ((effective_rating(p_rating_average, p_rating_count) - 1) / 4 * 40)
      -- Track record, saturating so a very busy pro cannot run away with it (0-20)
    + (least(coalesce(p_completed_jobs, 0), 50)::numeric / 50 * 20)
      -- Experience (0-10)
    + (least(coalesce(p_years_experience, 0), 15)::numeric / 15 * 10)
      -- Proximity: full marks within 5km, nothing beyond 50km (0-15)
    + (greatest(0, 50000 - least(coalesce(p_distance_meters, 50000), 50000) - 0)::numeric / 45000 * 15)
      -- Having actually said yes is the strongest signal available (0-10)
    + (case when p_has_expressed_interest then 10 else 0 end)
      -- Credentials on file (0-5)
    + (case when p_is_licensed_and_insured then 5 else 0 end)
  )::int));
procedure:public.pro_fit_score(numeric,i.definition:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.pro_fit_score(p_rating_average numeric, p_rating_count integer, p_completed_jobs integer, p_years_experience integer, p_distance_meters integer, p_has_expressed_interest boolean, p_is_licensed_and_insured boolean)
 RETURNS integer
 LANGUAGE sql
 IMMUTABLE
AS $function$
  select least(100, greatest(0, (
      -- Rating, blended (0-40)
      ((effective_rating(p_rating_average, p_rating_count) - 1) / 4 * 40)
      -- Track record, saturating so a very busy pro cannot run away with it (0-20)
    + (least(coalesce(p_completed_jobs, 0), 50)::numeric / 50 * 20)
      -- Experience (0-10)
    + (least(coalesce(p_years_experience, 0), 15)::numeric / 15 * 10)
      -- Proximity: full marks within 5km, nothing beyond 50km (0-15)
    + (greatest(0, 50000 - least(coalesce(p_distance_meters, 50000), 50000) - 0)::numeric / 45000 * 15)
      -- Having actually said yes is the strongest signal available (0-10)
    + (case when p_has_expressed_interest then 10 else 0 end)
      -- Credentials on file (0-5)
    + (case when p_is_licensed_and_insured then 5 else 0 end)
  )::int));
$function$

procedure:public.pro_open_windows(uuid,t.name: pro_open_windows
procedure:public.pro_open_windows(uuid,t.source_code:
with tz as (
    select coalesce(pr.timezone, 'America/Los_Angeles') as zone
    from profiles pr where pr.id = p_pro_id
  ),
  days as (
    select generate_series(
             (p_from at time zone (select zone from tz))::date - 1,
             (p_to   at time zone (select zone from tz))::date + 1,
             interval '1 day'
           )::date as d
  ),
  recurring as (
    select tstzrange(
             ((d + w.start_local_time) at time zone (select zone from tz)),
             ((d + w.end_local_time)   at time zone (select zone from tz)),
             '[)'
           ) as r
    from days
    join pro_weekly_availability w
      on w.pro_id = p_pro_id
     and w.is_enabled
     and w.day_of_week = extract(dow from days.d)::int
     and p_priority = any (w.priority_types)
  ),
  extra as (
    select o.time_range as r
    from pro_availability_overrides o
    where o.pro_id = p_pro_id
      and o.override_type in ('available', 'extra_hours')
  ),
  candidate as (
    select r from recurring
    union all
    select r from extra
  )
  select c.r
  from candidate c
  where c.r && tstzrange(p_from, p_to, '[)')
    -- Any blocking override removes the window.
    and not exists (
      select 1 from pro_availability_overrides o
      where o.pro_id = p_pro_id
        and o.override_type in ('unavailable', 'time_off', 'temporary_pause')
        and o.time_range && c.r
    );

 LANGUAGE sql
 STABLE
AS $function$
  with tz as (
    select coalesce(pr.timezone, 'America/Los_Angeles') as zone
    from profiles pr where pr.id = p_pro_id
  ),
  days as (
    select generate_series(
             (p_from at time zone (select zone from tz))::date - 1,
             (p_to   at time zone (select zone from tz))::date + 1,
             interval '1 day'
           )::date as d
  ),
  recurring as (
    select tstzrange(
             ((d + w.start_local_time) at time zone (select zone from tz)),
             ((d + w.end_local_time)   at time zone (select zone from tz)),
             '[)'
           ) as r
    from days
    join pro_weekly_availability w
      on w.pro_id = p_pro_id
     and w.is_enabled
     and w.day_of_week = extract(dow from days.d)::int
     and p_priority = any (w.priority_types)
  ),
  extra as (

    from pro_availability_overrides o
    where o.pro_id = p_pro_id
      and o.override_type in ('available', 'extra_hours')
  ),
  candidate as (
    select r from recurring
    union all
    select r from extra
  )
  select c.r
  from candidate c
  where c.r && tstzrange(p_from, p_to, '[)')
    -- Any blocking override removes the window.
    and not exists (

procedure:public.publish_job(uuid).name: publish_job
procedure:public.publish_job(uuid).definition:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.publish_job(p_job_id uuid)
 RETURNS TABLE(matches_created integer, pros_notified integer)
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public'
AS $function$
declare
  v_job       jobs%rowtype;
  v_created   int := 0;
  v_notified  int := 0;
  v_version   int;
begin
  -- Lock first. Everything after this is re-checked under the lock, so a
  -- concurrent publish cannot observe a stale precondition.
  select * into v_job from jobs where id = p_job_id for update;
  if not found then
    raise exception 'Job not found' using errcode = 'no_data_found';
  end if;

  -- Ownership, and deliberately NOT via is_trusted_context(). This function is
  -- itself SECURITY DEFINER, so current_user is always `postgres` inside it and
  -- a trusted-context check would be true for every caller — which silently
  -- disabled this check entirely until a test caught it. The predicate that
  -- means anything here is the caller's own identity.
  if v_job.customer_id <> auth.uid() and not is_admin() then
    raise exception 'Only the job owner may publish this job' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;

  if v_job.safety_classification = 'emergency_redirect' then
    raise exception 'An emergency-redirect job cannot be published'
      using errcode = 'invalid_parameter_value';
  end if;

  if v_job.diagnosis_id is null then
    raise exception 'Job has no completed diagnosis' using errcode = 'invalid_parameter_value';
  end if;

  if v_job.price_quote_id is null then
    raise exception 'Job has no locked price' using errcode = 'invalid_parameter_value';
  end if;

  -- Cancelled, assigned, completed and expired jobs are all rejected here.
  if v_job.status not in ('priced', 'published') then
    raise exception 'Job cannot be published from status %', v_job.status
      using errcode = 'invalid_parameter_value';
  end if;

  v_version := coalesce(v_job.priority_rule_version, 1);

  with eligible as (
    select e.pro_id, e.distance_meters
    from eligible_pros_for_job(p_job_id) e
    where v_job.requested_service_start is null
       or pro_is_available(
            e.pro_id, v_job.requested_service_start,
            v_job.estimated_duration_minutes, v_job.final_priority
          )
  ),
  inserted as (
    insert into job_matches (job_id, pro_id, status, distance_meters, job_version, eligibility_snapshot)
    select
      p_job_id, e.pro_id, 'eligible', e.distance_meters, v_version,
      jsonb_build_object(
        'category_id',        v_job.category_id,
        'priority',           v_job.final_priority,
        'distance_m',         e.distance_meters,
        'requires_docs',      v_job.requires_license_insurance,
        'required_skill_ids', v_job.required_skill_ids,
        'evaluated_at',       now()
      )
    from eligible e
    on conflict (job_id, pro_id) do nothing
    returning pro_id
  ),
  queued as (
    -- One event per pro per job version. The payload is display-safe: an id, a
    -- category, a rounded distance. No address, no customer, no price detail
    -- beyond what the pro is already entitled to see.
    insert into notification_outbox (
      recipient_user_id, event_type, entity_type, entity_id, event_version, priority, payload
    )
    select
      i.pro_id,
      'job_opportunity',
      'job',
      p_job_id,
      v_version,
      case v_job.final_priority when 'urgent' then 'high'::notification_priority
                                when 'soon'   then 'high'::notification_priority
                                else 'normal'::notification_priority end,
      jsonb_build_object(
        'job_id',      p_job_id,
        'category_id', v_job.category_id,
        'priority',    v_job.final_priority,
        'title',       v_job.title,
        'action_route', '/pro/opportunities/' || p_job_id
      )
    from inserted i
    on conflict (recipient_user_id, event_type, entity_id, event_version) do nothing
    returning 1
  )
  select
    (select count(*) from inserted),
    (select count(*) from queued)
  into v_created, v_notified;

  update jobs
     set status       = 'published',
         published_at = coalesce(published_at, now()),
         updated_at   = now()
   where id = p_job_id;

  insert into audit_events (actor_id, actor_kind, action, entity_type, entity_id, metadata)
  values (
    auth.uid(), 'system', 'job.published', 'job', p_job_id,
    jsonb_build_object(
      'matches_created', v_created,
      'pros_notified',   v_notified,
      'job_version',     v_version
    )
  );

  return query select v_created, v_notified;
end;
$function$

procedure:public.rate_limit_lock(text,pu.source_code:
-- One 64-bit key rather than the two-int form: the subject hash is 32 bytes,
  -- so folding it into a 32-bit half would collide far more often than it needs
  -- to, and a collision here means two unrelated devices serialize against each
  -- other.
  select pg_advisory_xact_lock(
    hashtextextended(p_action || ':' || p_scope::text || ':' || encode(p_hash, 'hex'), 0)
  );

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.register_device_token(p_token text, p_platform text, p_app_version text DEFAULT NULL::text)
 RETURNS void
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public'
AS $function$
begin
  if auth.uid() is null then
    raise exception 'Sign in first' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;
  if p_token is null or length(btrim(p_token)) = 0 then
    raise exception 'A device token is required'
      using errcode = 'invalid_parameter_value';
  end if;
  if p_platform not in ('ios','android','web') then
    raise exception 'Unknown platform %', p_platform
      using errcode = 'invalid_parameter_value';
  end if;

  insert into device_tokens (profile_id, token, platform, app_version)
  values (auth.uid(), btrim(p_token), p_platform, left(coalesce(p_app_version,''), 40))
  on conflict (token) do update
     set profile_id   = auth.uid(),
         platform     = excluded.platform,
         app_version  = excluded.app_version,
         last_seen_at = now(),
         -- Re-registering revives a token that was revoked at sign-out.
         revoked_at   = null;
end;
$function$

procedure:public.release_booking_and_reo.name: release_booking_and_reopen_job
procedure:public.release_booking_and_reo.source_code:
declare
  v_b        bookings%rowtype;
  v_job      jobs%rowtype;
  v_restored int := 0;
begin
  select * into v_b from bookings where id = p_booking_id;
  select * into v_job from jobs where id = v_b.job_id;

  update selection_attempts
     set outcome = p_outcome, outcome_reason = p_reason, resolved_at = now()
   where booking_id = p_booking_id and outcome = 'pending';

  -- The pro who declined or timed out is out for this job, in either mode.
  update job_matches
     set status = 'withdrawn', withdrawn_at = now(), updated_at = now()
   where job_id = v_b.job_id and pro_id = v_b.pro_id;

  if v_job.assignment_mode = 'marketplace' then
    -- Unchanged. Everyone who had said yes becomes selectable again — but only
    -- if they still qualify. A pro whose calendar filled or whose licence
    -- lapsed while the first choice was deciding must not silently return.
    with restorable as (
      select m.id
      from job_matches m
      join jobs j on j.id = m.job_id
      where m.job_id = v_b.job_id
        and m.status = 'not_selected'
        and m.available_start_at is not null
        and exists (select 1 from eligible_pros_for_job(v_b.job_id) e where e.pro_id = m.pro_id)
        and pro_is_available(m.pro_id, m.available_start_at,
                             j.estimated_duration_minutes, j.final_priority)
    )
    update job_matches m
       set status = 'interested', updated_at = now()
      from restorable r
     where m.id = r.id;
    get diagnostics v_restored = row_count;

    update jobs
       set status = 'published', closed_at = null, updated_at = now()
     where id = v_b.job_id;

  else
    -- Direct. The job goes back to the customer, not to the market.
    --
    -- Deliberately does NOT restore suppressed matches. If this job was
    -- converted from marketplace, those pros were told it closed; bringing them
    -- back silently would re-broadcast a job the customer has since chosen to
    -- handle privately. They return only when the customer explicitly calls
    -- publish_job_to_marketplace().
    --
    -- `priced` is the customer-action state: the locked price is untouched and
    -- still valid, and the customer can assign someone else or publish.
    update jobs
       set status = 'priced', closed_at = null, updated_at = now()
     where id = v_b.job_id;
  end if;

  -- Only the customer is told. In direct mode there is nobody else who knows.
  perform queue_booking_notification(p_booking_id, v_b.customer_id,
    case when p_outcome = 'expired' then 'pro_confirmation_timeout' else 'pro_declined' end,
    'high');

  insert into audit_events (actor_kind, action, entity_type, entity_id, metadata)
  values ('system', 'booking.released', 'booking', p_booking_id,
          jsonb_build_object(
            'outcome',          p_outcome,
            'reason',           p_reason,
            'job_id',           v_b.job_id,
            'assignment_mode',  v_job.assignment_mode,
            'matches_restored', v_restored,
            'job_returned_to',  case when v_job.assignment_mode = 'marketplace'
                                     then 'published' else 'priced' end));
end;
procedure:public.release_booking_and_reo.definition:

AS $function$

      where m.job_id = v_b.job_id
        and m.status = 'not_selected'
        and m.available_start_at is not null
        and exists (select 1 from eligible_pros_for_job(v_b.job_id) e where e.pro_id = m.pro_id)
        and pro_is_available(m.pro_id, m.available_start_at,
                             j.estimated_duration_minutes, j.final_priority)
    )
    update job_matches m
       set status = 'interested', updated_at = now()
      from restorable r
     where m.id = r.id;
    get diagnostics v_restored = row_count;

    update jobs
       set status = 'published', closed_at = null, updated_at = now()
     where id = v_b.job_id;

  else
    -- Direct. The job goes back to the customer, not to the market.
    --
    -- Deliberately does NOT restore suppressed matches. If this job was
    -- converted from marketplace, those pros were told it closed; bringing them
    -- back silently would re-broadcast a job the customer has since chosen to
    -- handle privately. They return only when the customer explicitly calls
    -- publish_job_to_marketplace().
    --
    -- `priced` is the customer-action state: the locked price is untouched and

    update jobs
       set status = 'priced', closed_at = null, updated_at = now()

  end if;

  -- Only the customer is told. In direct mode there is nobody else who knows.

  values ('system', 'booking.released', 'booking', p_booking_id,

            'reason',           p_reason,
            'job_id',           v_b.job_id,
            'assignment_mode',  v_job.assignment_mode,

                                     then 'published' else 'priced' end));
end;

procedure:public.sync_profile_identity().name: sync_profile_identity
procedure:public.sync_profile_identity().source_code:
begin
  update profiles p set
    is_anonymous = coalesce(new.is_anonymous, false),
    verified_at  = coalesce(
                     p.verified_at,
                     new.email_confirmed_at,
                     new.phone_confirmed_at
                   ),
    -- Set once, the first time a formerly anonymous account gains a
    -- confirmed identity. Re-running the upgrade must not move it.
    upgraded_at  = case
                     when p.upgraded_at is not null then p.upgraded_at
                     when p.is_anonymous
                      and coalesce(new.is_anonymous, false) = false
                      and coalesce(new.email_confirmed_at, new.phone_confirmed_at) is not null
                     then now()
                     else p.upgraded_at
                   end
  where p.id = new.id;
  return new;
end;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.sync_profile_identity()
 RETURNS trigger
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 SECURITY DEFINER
 SET search_path TO 'public'
AS $function$
begin
  update profiles p set

    verified_at  = coalesce(

declare
  v_id    uuid;
  v_first boolean;
begin
  if not is_trusted_caller() then
    raise exception 'Only the server may save a payment method'
      using errcode = '42501';
  end if;

  if p_stripe_pm_id is null or p_stripe_pm_id !~ '^pm_' then
    raise exception 'That is not a Stripe payment method id'
      using errcode = 'invalid_parameter_value', hint = 'bad_pm_id';
  end if;

  -- The first usable card a person saves becomes their default, because the
  -- alternative is a saved card that cannot be used until they visit a settings
  -- screen they have no reason to look for.
  select not exists (
    select 1 from payment_methods
     where profile_id = p_profile_id
       and detached_at is null
       and stripe_payment_method_id is distinct from p_stripe_pm_id
  ) into v_first;

  insert into payment_methods (profile_id, stripe_payment_method_id, brand, last4,
                               exp_month, exp_year, funding, is_default, livemode)
  values (p_profile_id, p_stripe_pm_id, p_brand, p_last4, p_exp_month, p_exp_year,
          coalesce(p_funding, 'unknown'), v_first, coalesce(p_livemode, false))
  on conflict (stripe_payment_method_id) do update
     set brand       = coalesce(excluded.brand, payment_methods.brand),
         last4       = coalesce(excluded.last4, payment_methods.last4),
         exp_month   = coalesce(excluded.exp_month, payment_methods.exp_month),
         exp_year    = coalesce(excluded.exp_year, payment_methods.exp_year),
         funding     = coalesce(excluded.funding, payment_methods.funding),
         -- A card that arrives again after being detached is attached again.
         detached_at = null,
         updated_at  = now()
  returning id into v_id;

  return v_id;
end;

procedure:realtime.apply_rls(jsonb,integ.source_code:
declare
    -- Regclass of the table e.g. public.notes
    entity_ regclass = (quote_ident(wal ->> 'schema') || '.' || quote_ident(wal ->> 'table'))::regclass;

    -- I, U, D, T: insert, update ...
    action realtime.action = (
        case wal ->> 'action'
            when 'I' then 'INSERT'
            when 'U' then 'UPDATE'
            when 'D' then 'DELETE'
            else 'ERROR'
        end
    );

    -- Is row level security enabled for the table
    is_rls_enabled bool = relrowsecurity from pg_class where oid = entity_;

    subscriptions realtime.subscription[] = array_agg(subs)
        from
            realtime.subscription subs
        where
            subs.entity = entity_
            -- Filter by action early - only get subscriptions interested in this action
            -- action_filter column can be: '*' (all), 'INSERT', 'UPDATE', or 'DELETE'
            and (subs.action_filter = '*' or subs.action_filter = action::text);

    -- Subscription vars
    working_role regrole;
    working_selected_columns text[];
    claimed_role regrole;
    claims jsonb;

    subscription_id uuid;
    subscription_has_access bool;
    visible_to_subscription_ids uuid[] = '{}';

    -- structured info for wal's columns
    columns realtime.wal_column[];
    -- previous identity values for update/delete
    old_columns realtime.wal_column[];

    error_record_exceeds_max_size boolean = octet_length(wal::text) > max_record_bytes;

    -- Primary jsonb output for record
    output jsonb;

    -- Loop record for iterating unique roles (outer loop)
    role_record record;
    -- Loop record for iterating unique selected_columns within a role (inner loop)
    cols_record record;
    -- Subscription ids visible at the role level (before fanning out by selected_columns)
    visible_role_sub_ids uuid[] = '{}';

begin
    perform set_config('role', null, true);

    columns =
        array_agg(
            (
                x->>'name',
                x->>'type',
                x->>'typeoid',
                realtime.cast(
                    (x->'value') #>> '{}',
                    coalesce(
                        (x->>'typeoid')::regtype, -- null when wal2json version <= 2.4
                        (x->>'type')::regtype
                    )
                ),
                (pks ->> 'name') is not null,
                true
            )::realtime.wal_column
        )
        from
            jsonb_array_elements(wal -> 'columns') x
            left join jsonb_array_elements(wal -> 'pk') pks
                on (x ->> 'name') = (pks ->> 'name');

    old_columns =
        array_agg(
            (
                x->>'name',
                x->>'type',
                x->>'typeoid',
                realtime.cast(
                    (x->'value') #>> '{}',
                    coalesce(
                        (x->>'typeoid')::regtype, -- null when wal2json version <= 2.4
                        (x->>'type')::regtype
                    )
                ),
                (pks ->> 'name') is not null,
                true
            )::realtime.wal_column
        )
        from
            jsonb_array_elements(wal -> 'identity') x
            left join jsonb_array_elements(wal -> 'pk') pks
                on (x ->> 'name') = (pks ->> 'name');

    for role_record in
        select claims_role
        from (select distinct claims_role from unnest(subscriptions)) t
        order by claims_role::text
    loop
        working_role := role_record.claims_role;

        -- Update `is_selectable` for columns and old_columns (once per role)
        columns =
            array_agg(
                (
                    c.name,
                    c.type_name,
                    c.type_oid,
                    c.value,
                    c.is_pkey,
                    pg_catalog.has_column_privilege(working_role, entity_, c.name, 'SELECT')
                )::realtime.wal_column
            )
            from
                unnest(columns) c;

        old_columns =
                array_agg(
                    (
                        c.name,
                        c.type_name,
                        c.type_oid,
                        c.value,
                        c.is_pkey,
                        pg_catalog.has_column_privilege(working_role, entity_, c.name, 'SELECT')
                    )::realtime.wal_column
                )
                from
                    unnest(old_columns) c;

        if action <> 'DELETE' and count(1) = 0 from unnest(columns) c where c.is_pkey then
            -- Fan out 400 error per distinct selected_columns for this role
            for cols_record in
                select selected_columns
                from (select distinct selected_columns from unnest(subscriptions) s where s.claims_role = working_role) t
                order by coalesce(array_to_string(selected_columns, ','), '')
            loop
                working_selected_columns := cols_record.selected_columns;
                return next (
                    jsonb_build_object(
                        'schema', wal ->> 'schema',
                        'table', wal ->> 'table',
                        'type', action
                    ),
                    is_rls_enabled,
                    (select array_agg(s.subscription_id) from unnest(subscriptions) as s where s.claims_role = working_role and (s.selected_columns is not distinct from working_selected_columns)),
                    array['Error 400: Bad Request, no primary key']
                )::realtime.wal_rls;
            end loop;

        -- The claims role does not have SELECT permission to the primary key of entity
        elsif action <> 'DELETE' and sum(c.is_selectable::int) <> count(1) from unnest(columns) c where c.is_pkey then
            -- Fan out 401 error per distinct selected_columns for this role
            for cols_record in
                select selected_columns
                from (select distinct selected_columns from unnest(subscriptions) s where s.claims_role = working_role) t
                order by coalesce(array_to_string(selected_columns, ','), '')
            loop
                working_selected_columns := cols_record.selected_columns;
                return next (
                    jsonb_build_object(
                        'schema', wal ->> 'schema',
                        'table', wal ->> 'table',
                        'type', action
                    ),
                    is_rls_enabled,
                    (select array_agg(s.subscription_id) from unnest(subscriptions) as s where s.claims_role = working_role and (s.selected_columns is not distinct from working_selected_columns)),
                    array['Error 401: Unauthorized']
                )::realtime.wal_rls;
            end loop;

        else
            -- Create the prepared statement (once per role)
            if is_rls_enabled and action <> 'DELETE' then
                if (select 1 from pg_prepared_statements where name = 'walrus_rls_stmt' limit 1) > 0 then
                    deallocate walrus_rls_stmt;
                end if;
                execute realtime.build_prepared_statement_sql('walrus_rls_stmt', entity_, columns);
            end if;

            -- Collect all visible subscription IDs for this role (filter check + RLS check)
            visible_role_sub_ids = '{}';

            for subscription_id, claims in (
                    select
                        subs.subscription_id,
                        subs.claims
                    from
                        unnest(subscriptions) subs
                    where
                        subs.entity = entity_
                        and subs.claims_role = working_role
                        and (
                            realtime.is_visible_through_filters(columns, subs.filters)
                            or (
                              action = 'DELETE'
                              and realtime.is_visible_through_filters(old_columns, subs.filters)
                            )
                        )
            ) loop

                if not is_rls_enabled or action = 'DELETE' then
                    visible_role_sub_ids = visible_role_sub_ids || subscription_id;
                else
                    -- Check if RLS allows the role to see the record
                    perform
                        -- Trim leading and trailing quotes from working_role because set_config
                        -- doesn't recognize the role as valid if they are included
                        set_config('role', trim(both '"' from working_role::text), true),
                        set_config('request.jwt.claims', claims::text, true);

                    execute 'execute walrus_rls_stmt' into subscription_has_access;

                    -- Reset the role on every FOR..LOOP batch execution.
                    -- The first batch of 10 rows is pre-fetched using the current connection role (PG internal behaviour)
                    -- then we have to reset it again otherwise it would use the role defined in the `set_config` above
                    -- to fetch the remaining rows when rows>10, which could be a user-defined role that lacks execution grants.
                    -- The flow is:
                    --   1. run batch with conn role
                    --   2. set_config working_role
                    --   3. execute walrus
                    --   4. reset role (revert)
                    --   5. repeat
                    perform set_config('role', null, true);

                    if subscription_has_access then
                        visible_role_sub_ids = visible_role_sub_ids || subscription_id;
                    end if;
                end if;
            end loop;

            perform set_config('role', null, true);

            -- Inner loop: per distinct selected_columns for this role
            for cols_record in
                select selected_columns
                from (select distinct selected_columns from unnest(subscriptions) s where s.claims_role = working_role) t
                order by coalesce(array_to_string(selected_columns, ','), '')
            loop
                working_selected_columns := cols_record.selected_columns;

                output = jsonb_build_object(
                    'schema', wal ->> 'schema',
                    'table', wal ->> 'table',
                    'type', action,
                    'commit_timestamp', to_char(
                        ((wal ->> 'timestamp')::timestamptz at time zone 'utc'),
                        'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"'
                    ),
                    'columns', (
                        select
                            jsonb_agg(
                                jsonb_build_object(
                                    'name', pa.attname,
                                    'type', pt.typname
                                )
                                order by pa.attnum asc
                            )
                        from
                            pg_attribute pa
                            join pg_type pt
                                on pa.atttypid = pt.oid
                            left join (
                                select unnest(conkey) as pkey_attnum
                                from pg_constraint
                                where conrelid = entity_ and contype = 'p'
                            ) pk on pk.pkey_attnum = pa.attnum
                        where
                            attrelid = entity_
                            and attnum > 0
                            and pg_catalog.has_column_privilege(working_role, entity_, pa.attname, 'SELECT')
                            and (working_selected_columns is null or pa.attname = any(working_selected_columns) or pk.pkey_attnum is not null)
                    )
                )
                -- Add "record" key for insert and update
                || case
                    when action in ('INSERT', 'UPDATE') then
                        jsonb_build_object(
                            'record',
                            (
                                select
                                    jsonb_object_agg(
                                        -- if unchanged toast, get column name and value from old record
                                        coalesce((c).name, (oc).name),
                                        case
                                            when (c).name is null then (oc).value
                                            else (c).value
                                        end
                                    )
                                from
                                    unnest(columns) c
                                    full outer join unnest(old_columns) oc
                                        on (c).name = (oc).name
                                where
                                    coalesce((c).is_selectable, (oc).is_selectable)
                                    and (working_selected_columns is null or coalesce((c).name, (oc).name) = any(working_selected_columns) or coalesce((c).is_pkey, (oc).is_pkey))
                                    and ( not error_record_exceeds_max_size or (octet_length((c).value::text) <= 64))
                            )
                        )
                    else '{}'::jsonb
                end
                -- Add "old_record" key for update and delete
                || case
                    when action = 'UPDATE' then
                        jsonb_build_object(
                                'old_record',
                                (
                                    select jsonb_object_agg((c).name, (c).value)
                                    from unnest(old_columns) c
                                    where
                                        (c).is_selectable
                                        and (working_selected_columns is null or (c).name = any(working_selected_columns) or (c).is_pkey)
                                        and ( not error_record_exceeds_max_size or (octet_length((c).value::text) <= 64))
                                )
                            )
                    when action = 'DELETE' then
                        jsonb_build_object(
                            'old_record',
                            (
                                select jsonb_object_agg((c).name, (c).value)
                                from unnest(old_columns) c
                                where
                                    (c).is_selectable
                                    and (working_selected_columns is null or (c).name = any(working_selected_columns) or (c).is_pkey)
                                    and ( not error_record_exceeds_max_size or (octet_length((c).value::text) <= 64))
                                    and ( not is_rls_enabled or (c).is_pkey ) -- if RLS enabled, we can't secure deletes so filter to pkey
                            )
                        )
                    else '{}'::jsonb
                end;

                -- Filter visible_role_sub_ids to those matching the current selected_columns group
                visible_to_subscription_ids = coalesce(
                    (
                        select array_agg(s.subscription_id)
                        from unnest(subscriptions) s
                        where s.claims_role = working_role
                          and (s.selected_columns is not distinct from working_selected_columns)
                          and s.subscription_id = any(visible_role_sub_ids)
                    ),
                    '{}'::uuid[]
                );

                return next (
                    output,
                    is_rls_enabled,
                    visible_to_subscription_ids,
                    case
                        when error_record_exceeds_max_size then array['Error 413: Payload Too Large']
                        else '{}'
                    end
                )::realtime.wal_rls;
            end loop;

        end if;
    end loop;

    perform set_config('role', null, true);
end;
